correctness.rationale: A vector spells a linear word exactly via an Euler trail: each active vertex lies in one weak component, with balanced degrees or the unique +1,−1 pair. In the loopless graph every directed cycle uses both 01 and 10, and every edge touches at least one of these. Any separate balanced active component must have a cycle; a nonzero imbalance pair cannot be split across components because each component's total imbalance is zero. Thus the nonloop support is connected when nonempty. A loop may be added only at an incident vertex, except for the two one-vertex loop-only families. The degree equations, threshold f≥max(0,d−b−u), and loop boundary corrections then count each feasible vector once, with the empty vector included exactly once. In a separate exact algebra replay, grouping b and d by zero versus positive and summing on the signed difference of their excesses reproduces the full rational identity; an appended-bit suffix/profile DP also agrees through n=44. Replay: `python /workspace/independent_checks_1_4.py 3`. The pole at 1 gives (13/12)/4!=13/288, and choosing one word per profile proves the exact codebook bound. The finite DP is corroboration, not extrapolation.
